source_reachability:
All fetched by me on 2026-09-16 with curl -A "Mokaair-editorial"; every body was opened and checked, not just the status code.

SOURCE 1 https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/devices/pixel/september-2026-pixel-drop/ — HTTP 200, 389,352 bytes, server "Google Frontend". Real document: JSON-LD NewsArticle, og/twitter meta, full article body, self-canonical. Also discoverable in blog.google/rss/ under the exact title, so the URL was not guessed.

SOURCE 2 https://support.google.com/pixelphone/thread/466181739 — HTTP 200, 2,060,182 bytes. Real document. Body is NOT in plain HTML: it sits in a double-escaped inline-JSON blob and only appears after unescaping \uXXXX/\xXX. Linked from the blog's words "community forum post".

SOURCE 3 https://support.google.com/googlepixelwatch/thread/464268922 — HTTP 200, 1,898,242 bytes. Real document, same decoding needed. Linked from the blog's words "Pixel Watch".

SOURCE 4 https://support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/16704479 — HTTP 200, 1,681,250 bytes, canonical .../answer/16704479?hl=en. Reached directly AND independently via Google's own link https://support.google.com/pixelphone?p=scam_detection, which I followed to 200 at answer/16704479. The answer id was therefore not guessed.

SUPPORTING (not sources): answer/16704479?hl=zh-Hant 200 (carries Google's own 「這個頁面可能含有使用 AI 技術翻譯的內容，也許會有錯誤」); matrix attachment PNG 200, 73,292 bytes, 1743x629; second thread attachment PNG 200, 2312x1301; source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/pixel-watch 200; audible.com/ep/pixel-country-selection 200; blog.google/.../android/pause-point/ 200 (datePublished 2026-05-12T17:00:00+00:00, meta authors "Sophie Sanders"); blog.google/.../november-2025-pixel-drop/ 200; blog.google/intl/zh-tw/<this post> 404; blog.google/intl/zh-tw/ 200; sibling watch threads 442344064 / 414486587 / 417704094 all 200.

No 403, no challenge page, no "Access Denied" body anywhere. NO source or fact traces to a news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet — all four sources are Google-owned properties. No URL, build number or identifier in the record is one the researcher could only have guessed.

My fact-check JSON: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-travel-scanner/7f63d65a-c509-5a16-8b56-4ffddc3bb57b/scratchpad/research/tech-news-pixel-drop-20260915-factcheck.json (researcher's own file left intact, backed up alongside as ...-researcher-backup.json, matching the convention already used in that directory).

refuted.fact: not_said[11]: "blog.google's related-stories rail shows a separate 'September Android Drop' post; the Pixel Drop note does not reference it."
refuted.why: REFUTED. The string 'Android Drop' occurs ZERO times in the page I fetched. The related-stories rail lists exactly four items: 'You can officially buy the Pixel 11 phones and Pixel Watch 5.'; 'Here's how to use sign-to-text translation on Pixel 11.' (Sharlene Yuan); 'Get closer to the game with Gemini and Pixel' (Eileen Mannion); 'Stay present while taking pictures with Magic Capture on Pixel 11.' A probe URL for a September 2026 Android Drop post returns 404. Delete the sentence — as written it invites the writer to mention a post I cannot show exists.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[1]: 'The browser-tab/og title is shorter: September Pixel Drop: VIP updates, Pixel Watch features.'
refuted.why: REFUTED in part. og:title AND twitter:title both carry the FULL headline 'September Pixel Drop: New Pixel VIP updates, Pixel Watch features, and more'. Only the <title> element is the short form. Calling it the 'og title' is wrong.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[36]: 'Four example actions are named' for Offline Gemini.
refuted.why: REFUTED. Google names three — 'setting up a timer, starting/stopping a workout, turning on do not disturb' — followed by the catch-all 'and other device actions', which is not a named action. Must be three plus an open-ended tail.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[26]: footnote 5 is 'the only availability caveat Google attaches to the VIP widget and Harry Potter rows'.
refuted.why: REFUTED in part. Disclaimer 2 also constrains the Harry Potter row: 'Harry Potter Audiobook Packs available until December 31, 2026.' The claim holds only for the Pixel VIPs row (and Pause Point), not for Harry Potter.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[12]: '...so the five named features are explicitly not the complete list.'
refuted.why: REFUTED as a count. The prose under 'Here are just some of the features to look forward to' carries FOUR feature headings: 'Pixel VIPs updates', 'Harry Potter Audiobook Packs', 'Scam Detection comes to your keyboard and expands to new regions', 'Pause Point expands to more Pixel devices'. Five is the ROW count of the availability image, where Scam Detection is split into two rows. Writing 「Google 列出五項功能」 would not match Google's prose.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[40]: the watch note 'ends its feature list with General bug fixes and improvements, is signed Thanks, Google Pixel Watch Support Team'.
unsupported.why: The sign-off is real but sits near the TOP of the note, immediately after the security-bulletin line — not at the end. The note ends with 'Previous Pixel Watch Updates'. The phrasing implies a closing signature that is not there.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[41]: 'lists Google's previous Pixel Watch updates of 2026'.
unsupported.why: The visible labels read only 'June (Pixel Watch 2, 3, & 4)', 'March EMR (Pixel Watch 1)', 'March (Pixel Watch 2, 3, & 4)'. No year is written anywhere in the note. The year is carried only by the link URLs (.../google-pixel-watch-update-june-2026, .../google-pixel-watch-update-march-2026, .../pixel-watch-1-modem-software-update-march-2026), which I confirmed but which the researcher never cited. Keep the fact, attribute the year to the hrefs.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[20]: the note 'links back to Google's own November 2025 Pixel Drop post as its origin'.
unsupported.why: The href is confirmed (blog.google/products-and-platforms/devices/pixel/november-2025-pixel-drop/, HTTP 200) but Google never says the feature originated there. 'as its origin' is the researcher's inference, not the source's statement. Write 'links to Google's November 2025 Pixel Drop post'.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[35]: recorded verbatim quote for Proactive suggestions.
unsupported.why: The quote stops at 'surfaces it directly on your wrist' with no ellipsis; the source continues ', eliminating the need to dig through your phone'. Meaning is unchanged but it is not verbatim-complete, and verbatim_quote fields are what a translator copies.

additional_findings: WATCH-NOTE DATE — the researcher's biggest missed opportunity, and it flips an exclusion into a usable finding. The researcher decoded the watch thread's internal timestamps (2026-09-01T19:47:42Z post, 2026-09-03T17:28:18Z later activity) but excluded them as 'undocumented internal fields'. I calibrated that field and it is reliable: thread 442344064 'Google Pixel Watch Update - June 2026' = 2026-06-16, thread 414486587 'Google Pixel Watch Update - March 2026' = 2026-03-03, thread 417704094 'Pixel Watch 1 Modem Software Update - March 2026' = 2026-03-16 — and two of those match the Pixel Watch security bulletin's own published dates EXACTLY (June 2026 bulletin published June 16 2026; March 2026 bulletin published March 3 2026). So the Pixel Watch 5 / Wear OS 7 note predates the Pixel Drop blog post by about two weeks. The researcher's practical instruction ('do NOT write that the Pixel Watch 5 Wear OS 7 update was announced on 15 September') is correct and should be promoted from unverified_or_excluded into must_not_write. CAUTION: do not print 2026-09-01 as a fact either — the note quotes build CP3A.260905.002, whose 260905 stamp is later than 2026-09-01, so the note was evidently edited after posting. Say only that Google published the watch note before the Drop post and gives it no visible date.

DATE CONFIRMATION, the other direction — the same field on the Pixel Drop phone thread decodes to 2026-09-15T18:27:40Z, 27 minutes after the blog post's 18:00:00Z datePublished. event_date 2026-09-15 and the slug suffix 20260915 are now doubly confirmed, not just from the blog's JSON-LD.

HELP CENTRE HAS NO DATE — support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/16704479 carries no visible publication or update date, no dateModified, no JSON-LD; the only 'Last updated' strings in the file are JavaScript template literals. So the 11 regions / 8 languages can only be described as the page state read on 2026-09-16, never as 'after the September Drop'. Belongs in not_said; the record does not have it.

HELP CENTRE STATES NO MODEL CONDITION — its 'Check feature eligibility' section lists regions and languages ONLY. It states no Pixel model requirement for chat Scam Detection, although the forum note says 'Pixel 6 and newer' and the matrix starts at Pixel 6/6a. Two Google pages give different eligibility scopes; the record does not note this, and it is a reason not to present the Help Centre list as complete eligibility.

MATERIAL OMISSION, CIRCLE TO SEARCH / GOOGLE LENS — a whole section of the cited Help Centre page is absent from the entire research record: 'Use Circle to Search & Google Lens to spot scam messages', with step lists for both and the sentence 'Our systems will use AI and information from the web to assess whether the message is likely a scam.' Google attaches NO region or language restriction to this route. For a Taiwan-facing article this is the single most useful thing on the page, because it is the one scam-checking route Google does not fence behind the 11-region list. It should be recorded — but flagged as an AI/web-lookup feature, expressly unlike the on-device Scam Detection, so the two are not blurred.

THREE DIFFERENT 'SCAM DETECTION' THINGS ON ONE PAGE — the same Help Centre page also documents call-level Scam Detection ('On eligible Pixel phones, you can get real-time alerts if a call shows patterns commonly associated with scams') and Google Messages spam ('The Google Messages app automatically detects and moves suspected spam into a dedicated folder'). Neither is in the record. 'Scam Detection' in this Drop means the chat-notification and keyboard variants only; the article must not conflate the three.

FORUM NOTE LINK TARGETS — 'Update to the latest Android version' -> support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/7680439 and 'update your apps' -> support.google.com/googleplay/answer/113412. These confirm verified_facts[11]'s two-channel inference with Google's own hrefs rather than by reading between the lines.

SECOND ATTACHMENT — the phone thread carries a second image the record does not mention: thread-466181739-10255076335878498553.png, 'Gstore_1156 x 650.5.png', 1,195,593 bytes, 2312x1301. It is thread hero art, not a data table. Recorded so a later agent does not mistake it for a second matrix.

DEVICE MATRIX INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED, AND IT HOLDS — I detected the grid lines and counted dark pixels inside every cell rather than trusting a visual read. Result: 25 device columns in exactly the order the researcher recorded, 5 feature rows as recorded, and in every one of the five rows cells 1-24 contain a tick glyph (30-35 dark pixels) while cell 25, Pixel Tablet, contains 0. The duplicated 'DE' in '(AR, DE, ES, FR, DE, PT, and JA)' is confirmed at 6x and is Google's own defect. This is the part of the record most likely to be wrong and it is exactly right.

EVERY HARD NUMBER CHECKS OUT — 9 countries, 6 languages, 11 cumulative regions, 8 cumulative languages, 10 Audible countries, both expiry dates (packs 2026-12-31, Audible offer 2027-01-14), build CP3A.260905.002, 8 hand gestures, all five footnote-to-disclaimer mappings, and the zh-Hant UI strings (設定 > 安全性與隱私權 > 其他安全性和隱私權設定 > 詐騙偵測 > 訊息詐騙; 疑似詐騙) are all verbatim-correct. not_said[14] (no September 2026 Pixel Watch bulletin; newest is August 2026, published August 20 2026, patch level 2026-08-05, footer 'Last updated 2026-08-20 UTC'), not_said[15] (zh-tw post 404) and the Audible country-picker exclusion (12 locale entries, no trial terms, unrelated $0.99/mo banner) all hold too. Verdict is needs_fixes only because of the eight items above, not because the substance is unsound.
